headline: South Korean Researchers Develop Contact Lenses That Heal Themselves
meta_description: New UV-activated contact lenses repair scratches in under an hour, reducing waste and replacement costs for millions of users worldwide.
summary_short: South Korean researchers have created contact lenses that automatically repair scratches when exposed to sunlight, potentially transforming vision care.
body:
Researchers Jung-Hyun Choi and Byung-Ki Cho have developed a breakthrough contact lens technology that repairs surface scratches on its own when exposed to UV light—a discovery that could transform how millions manage their vision care. The innovation uses a UV-activated hydrogel that heals small imperfections in under an hour, eliminating the expense and inconvenience of replacement. At a wavelength of 365 nanometers, ultraviolet light triggers a process called disulfide exchange, temporarily breaking apart sulfur bonds in the gel so they can reconnect with neighboring atoms, effectively sealing scratches. Before-and-after photographs from the study demonstrate how these new molecular connections leave barely visible traces on the lens surface.

What makes this advancement particularly practical is its versatility. The researchers explain that home repairs could eventually become routine—users might harness UV light from nail polish curing devices or indoor grow lamps for houseplants to restore their lenses. Beyond the self-healing capability, the new lenses feature an additional polymer layer that resists bacterial buildup and abrasion, even withstanding repeated contact with sandpaper. The material also retains moisture better than commercially available alternatives.

Testing revealed that repaired scratches achieved only a 2% perceptibility score, meaning multiple repairs could be performed before transparency issues would necessitate replacement. This durability translates directly to reduced waste and lower costs for contact lens wearers everywhere. While the technology still awaits South Korean regulatory approval before market testing can begin, the study—published in ACS Applied Polymer Materials and partly funded by the National Research Foundation of South Korea—represents a meaningful step toward more sustainable and economical vision solutions.
quick_facts: Developed by South Korean researchers Jung-Hyun Choi and Byung-Ki Cho
UV light at 365 nanometers wavelength triggers the self-healing process
Scratches repair completely in under one hour of exposure
Repaired scratches score only 2% perceptibility, allowing multiple repairs
Could eventually be repaired at home using nail polish UV lamps
